questions.q: Why are Scheduled Jobs one of the most common real-world causes of semaphore contention?
options: They run as background work, drawing from the same limited semaphore pool reserved for that category on each node
Scheduled Jobs do not use any node resources at all
Scheduled Jobs are exempt from every semaphore limit by default
They only run once per year, so contention is rare
questions.explain: Scheduled Jobs are background work, which competes for the same bounded background-processing semaphore pool other background work also needs.

questions.q: What are the two distinct ways Scheduled Jobs create contention, per this lesson?
options: Simultaneity (many jobs starting at the exact same time) and duration (one job running far longer than it should)
Only the number of fields on the Scheduled Job form
Only which user created the Scheduled Job
Only whether the job is marked active or inactive
questions.explain: Too many jobs clustered at one start time, and any single job with an excessively long runtime, are two separate real causes.

questions.q: Why can a well-optimized Job B still run late because of an unrelated Job A?
options: Job A is still occupying a semaphore slot Job B needs, so Job B waits regardless of its own code quality
Job B's script must always be broken if it runs late
Job A and Job B must always be editing the same table
Scheduled Jobs never actually affect each other
questions.explain: The delay has nothing to do with Job B's own code — it's resource contention for a shared, limited pool, exactly as Lesson 13 described.

questions.q: What is the practical fix for jobs that all start at the exact same time?
options: Stagger their start times across a wider window instead of clustering them at one moment
Disable all Scheduled Jobs permanently
Rewrite every job's script regardless of runtime
Move all jobs to run only on weekends
questions.explain: Staggering addresses simultaneity directly, without needing to touch any job's underlying script.

questions.q: If staggering start times doesn't fully solve the contention, what else should be investigated, and how does it connect to earlier course content?
options: The individual job with an unusually long runtime, using the script-diagnosis skills taught in Chapter 2 of this course
The user's browser cache, since that's unrelated to server-side scheduling
The Instance Health dashboard's color scheme
Nothing further can be done once jobs are staggered
questions.explain: A long-running job occupies its semaphore slot longer regardless of when it starts — fixing its script (Chapter 2 skills) shrinks that occupancy time.
